definition: An opponent or enemy in a contest, conflict, dispute, or game.
definition_zh: 對手；敵手；仇敵

mnemonic.story_en: Your ADVERSARY is the person who has VERT (turned) AD (toward) you to fight against you.
mnemonic.story_zh: 轉過身（VERS）面向（AD）你的人，就是你必須在戰場上面對的「對手」。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to, toward; connect this root idea with adversary.

example: Despite being an old political adversary, he paid tribute to the deceased prime minister.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 adversary 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: opponent is related, but adversary has its own usage pattern and context.
rival may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with adversary.

usage_note: adversary is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To make suffering, deficiency, or a problem less severe or more bearable.
definition_zh: 減輕；緩和；緩解

mnemonic.story_en: Doctors try to ALLEVIATE pain by using medicine to make the heavy burden LEVI (light).
mnemonic.story_zh: 醫生開藥是為了「減輕」痛苦，讓原本沉重的病情變得輕（LEVI）一些。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to; connect this root idea with alleviate.

example: The government introduced new tax cuts to alleviate the financial burden on middle-class families.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 alleviate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: relieve is related, but alleviate has its own usage pattern and context.
mitigate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with alleviate.

usage_note: alleviate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To make minor changes in a text, law, or agreement in order to make it fairer, more accurate, or more up-to-date.
definition_zh: 修訂；修正（法規、文本等）；改進

mnemonic.story_en: To AMEND a constitution means to remove old MENDA (faults) and update it with correct rules.
mnemonic.story_zh: 修改法律（AMEND）的核心在於剔除（EX）原本的瑕疵與錯誤（MENDA），使其更臻完美。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX- = out; connect this root idea with amend.

example: The committee voted unanimously to amend the constitution to allow online voting.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 amend 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: modify is related, but amend has its own usage pattern and context.
revise may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with amend.

usage_note: amend is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To assess the value, quality, or performance of something or someone, typically in an official or professional capacity.
definition_zh: 評估；估價；評價

mnemonic.story_en: An expert will APPRAISE the antique by looking at it closely to assign a fair PRETIUM (price).
mnemonic.story_zh: 古董專家在「估價（APPRAISE）」時，會仔細觀察並對其定出一個合理的價格（PRETIUM）。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to, toward; connect this root idea with appraise.

example: Managers will appraise the performance of each employee during the annual review next week.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 appraise 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: evaluate is related, but appraise has its own usage pattern and context.
assess may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with appraise.

usage_note: appraise is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Having or showing the ability to speak fluently, clearly, and coherently, especially in expressing complex ideas.
definition_zh: 口才流利的；表達清晰的；發音清晰的

mnemonic.story_en: An ARTICULATE speaker connects thoughts together smoothly, just as functional ARTICULUS (joints) connect bones.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個「說話清晰流利」的人，能把文字像關節（ARTICULUS）一樣，一節一節完美銜接、表達流暢。
mnemonic.root_memory: ARTICULUS = small joint, division; connect this root idea with articulate.

example: She is an articulate defender of human rights, capable of swaying large crowds with her speeches.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 articulate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: eloquent is related, but articulate has its own usage pattern and context.
fluent may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with articulate.

usage_note: articulate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully; to cause others to recognize one's authority or rights.
definition_zh: 堅稱；斷言；維護（權利、權威）

mnemonic.story_en: When you ASSERT your rights, you SERERE (bind) your words tightly AD (to) your personal authority.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「堅稱」或「維護」權利時，就像是把自己的立場牢牢綁定（SERERE）在某個立場上，絕不退讓。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD- = to; connect this root idea with assert.

example: The company legal team continues to assert that no patents were violated during development.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 assert 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: declare is related, but assert has its own usage pattern and context.
maintain may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with assert.

usage_note: assert is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Gentle and kindly; (of a disease or tumor) not harmful in effect, not malignant.
definition_zh: 慈祥的；溫和的；（腫瘤）良性的

mnemonic.story_en: The doctor smiled because the test showed a BENIGN tumor, meaning it was BENE (good) and not deadly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根 BENE 代表「好」。醫生告訴病人腫瘤是「良性的（BENIGN）」，意味著它不會帶來壞影響。
mnemonic.root_memory: BENE = well, good; connect this root idea with benign.

example: The biopsy indicated that the lump was benign, relieving the anxious patient immensely.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 benign 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: harmless is related, but benign has its own usage pattern and context.
kindly may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with benign.

usage_note: benign is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A system of government or administration in which most of the important decisions are made by state officials rather than by elected representatives, often characterized by red tape.
definition_zh: 官僚體制；官僚作風；繁文縟節

mnemonic.story_en: In a heavy BUREAUCRACY, power (KRATOS) belongs to the people sitting behind a BUREAU (office desk).
mnemonic.story_zh: 由辦公桌（BUREAU）和權力（KRATOS）結合而成，指「坐在辦公桌後的官員掌握統治權」，多用來諷刺效率低下的體制。
mnemonic.root_memory: BUREAU = desk, office; connect this root idea with bureaucracy.

example: Small business owners often complain about the excessive corporate bureaucracy required to get a simple permit.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 bureaucracy 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: administration is related, but bureaucracy has its own usage pattern and context.
red tape may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with bureaucracy.

usage_note: bureaucracy is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because it is illicit, illegal, or unauthorized.
definition_zh: 秘密的；暗中的；私下的（尤指違法活動）

mnemonic.story_en: The spies held a CLANDESTINE meeting in a dark room, keeping their words hidden like a closed CLAM.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根 CLAM 意為秘密。把秘密會議想像成緊閉的蚌殼（clam），在暗中「秘密」進行，不為外人所知。
mnemonic.root_memory: CLAM = secretly, in secret; connect this root idea with clandestine.

example: The intelligence agency uncovered a clandestine operation to smuggle high-tech weapons across the border.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 clandestine 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: secret is related, but clandestine has its own usage pattern and context.
covert may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with clandestine.

usage_note: clandestine is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The practice of persuading someone to do something by using force or threats.
definition_zh: 強迫；脅迫；高壓統治

mnemonic.story_en: The dictator used COERCION, bringing forces together (CO) to enclose and restrain (ARCERE) the citizens' freedom.
mnemonic.story_zh: 透過把所有人聚在一起（CO）並加以限制與圍困（ARCERE），達到「強迫」他人服從的目的。
mnemonic.root_memory: CO- = together; connect this root idea with coercion.

example: The confession was thrown out of court because the judge found it was obtained through police coercion.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 coercion 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: compulsion is related, but coercion has its own usage pattern and context.
force may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with coercion.

usage_note: coercion is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Relating to the mental action or process of acquiring knowledge and understanding through thought, experience, and the senses.
definition_zh: 認知的；大腦意識的

mnemonic.story_en: COGNITIVE development in children refers to how they grow to COGNOSCERE (know) and understand the world.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根 COGNOSCERE 代表去認識。COGNITIVE 便是與人類大腦如何「認知」、獲取知識有關的形容詞。
mnemonic.root_memory: COGNOSCERE = to get to know, recognize; connect this root idea with cognitive.

example: As people age, keeping the mind active with puzzles can help delay cognitive decline.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 cognitive 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: mental is related, but cognitive has its own usage pattern and context.
intellectual may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with cognitive.

usage_note: cognitive is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To work jointly on an activity or project, especially to produce or create something.
definition_zh: 合作；協作；共同編寫

mnemonic.story_en: To COLLABORATE means to bring people together (COM) to LABOR (work) on a single project.
mnemonic.story_zh: 由 COM（共同）和 LABOR（工作）組成，意思非常直白，就是「共同工作、合作」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with collaborate.

example: Researchers from three different universities collaborated to publish the groundbreaking medical study.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 collaborate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: cooperate is related, but collaborate has its own usage pattern and context.
team up may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with collaborate.

usage_note: collaborate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold, such as copper or coffee; a useful or valuable thing.
definition_zh: 商品；日用品；有價值的物品

mnemonic.story_en: A COMMODITY provides a COMMODUS (convenient) solution for buyers who need raw materials like oil or corn.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源於拉丁文的「合適與方便（COMMODUS）」。能夠交易並為大眾生活帶來便利的大宗物資，就被稱為「商品（COMMODITY）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COMMODUS = convenient, suitable, proper; connect this root idea with commodity.

example: In today's fast-paced corporate culture, time has become a highly valuable commodity.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 commodity 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: product is related, but commodity has its own usage pattern and context.
good may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with commodity.

usage_note: commodity is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Able to exist, occur, or work together without problems or conflict; consistent.
definition_zh: 相容相稱的；能共處的；合得來的

mnemonic.story_en: Two COMPATIBLE software programs can run together (COM) and endure (PATI) the workload without crashing.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字面意思是「能在一起（COM）互相包容與經受考驗（PATI）」，引申為軟體或人際關係間的「相容、合得來」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with compatible.

example: The new operating system update is fully compatible with older hardware models.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 compatible 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: harmonious is related, but compatible has its own usage pattern and context.
consistent may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with compatible.

usage_note: compatible is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To produce something (such as a list, report, or book) by assembling information collected from other sources.
definition_zh: 彙編；編輯；收集（資料）

mnemonic.story_en: To COMPILE data, you gather pages together (COM) and heap them up (PILARE) into an organized folder.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把分散在各處的資料收集起來（COM），像堆木頭一樣堆疊（PILARE）並整理在一起，就是「彙編、編纂」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with compile.

example: The research assistant spent weeks trying to compile a comprehensive database of historical climate records.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 compile 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: assemble is related, but compile has its own usage pattern and context.
gather may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with compile.

usage_note: compile is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The action or fact of complying with a wish, command, rule, or law; formal obedience or conformity.
definition_zh: 順從；服從；（對法規的）遵守、符合

mnemonic.story_en: The factory remained in full COMPLIANCE because they fulfilled (PLERE) and satisfied completely (COM) all safety laws.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自 comply（遵守）。字面意思是完全（COM）填滿（PLERE）法規的要求，達到「符合、遵守法規」的狀態。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = completely; connect this root idea with compliance.

example: The company was fined $50,000 for failing to maintain compliance with environmental regulations.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 compliance 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: obedience is related, but compliance has its own usage pattern and context.
conformity may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with compliance.

usage_note: compliance is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To admit that something is true or valid after first denying or resisting it; to surrender or yield a right or possession.
definition_zh: （勉強）承認；讓步；退讓；承認（失敗）

mnemonic.story_en: After realizing he lost the election, the candidate chose to CONCEDE and formally yield (CEDERE) victory to his opponent.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當局勢已定，不得不完全（COM）退讓（CEDERE），這就是「（勉強）承認失敗」或「讓步」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = completely; connect this root idea with concede.

example: The candidate refused to concede the election until every single ballot had been counted.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 concede 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: admit is related, but concede has its own usage pattern and context.
acknowledge may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with concede.

usage_note: concede is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To be of the same opinion; to agree; to happen or take place at the same time.
definition_zh: 同意、意見一致；同時發生

mnemonic.story_en: The board members CONCUR with the plan, meaning their thoughts run (CURRERE) together (COM) in perfect agreement.
mnemonic.story_zh: 大家的思緒與腳步一起（COM）向前奔跑（CURRERE），朝同一個方向前進，即代表「意見一致、同意」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with concur.

example: The medical board heavily concurred with the findings of the initial diagnostic report.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 concur 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: agree is related, but concur has its own usage pattern and context.
coincide may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with concur.

usage_note: concur is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To make something denser or more concentrated; to express a piece of writing or speech in fewer words.
definition_zh: 濃縮；壓縮（文字等）；（氣體）凝結

mnemonic.story_en: The editor asked him to CONDENSE the book, squeezing the pages to make the plot DENSUS (thick and compact).
mnemonic.story_zh: 完全（COM）將字句或分子擠壓得更加緊密（DENSUS），將多餘部分去掉，就是「濃縮」或「凝結」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = completely; connect this root idea with condense.

example: You need to condense this 50-page report into a brief two-page executive summary.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 condense 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: summarize is related, but condense has its own usage pattern and context.
compress may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with condense.

usage_note: condense is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: An idea or feeling that a word invokes for a person in addition to its literal or primary meaning (denotation).
definition_zh: 內涵意義；言外之意；隱含意義

mnemonic.story_en: The word 'cheap' has a negative CONNOTATION, because it brings a bad feeling together with (COM) its basic NOTA (note/meaning).
mnemonic.story_zh: 除了字面上的主要記號（NOTARE）之外，單字本身「一同（COM）帶來的弦外之音或情感色彩」，就是「內涵/隱含意義」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together with; connect this root idea with connotation.

example: The word 'cheap' has a negative connotation, whereas 'inexpensive' sounds much more positive.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 connotation 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: implication is related, but connotation has its own usage pattern and context.
nuance may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with connotation.

usage_note: connotation is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A general agreement among a group of people; shared opinion or collective judgment.
definition_zh: 共識；一致的意見

mnemonic.story_en: To reach a CONSENSUS, all committee members must feel (SENTIRE) the same way together (COM) about the issue.
mnemonic.story_zh: 群體在一起（COM）思考並擁有相同的感受（SENTIRE），這就是「達成共識」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with consensus.

example: After hours of heated debate, the board finally reached a consensus on the new budget plan.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 consensus 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: agreement is related, but consensus has its own usage pattern and context.
unanimity may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with consensus.

usage_note: consensus is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A member of a constituency; a voter in a specific district represented by an elected official; also, a component part of something.
definition_zh: 選民、選區居民；成分、構成要素

mnemonic.story_en: Politicians must listen to each CONSTITUENT, because these voters stand together (COM) to set up (STATUERE) the government.
mnemonic.story_zh: 共同（COM）站出來建立（STATUERE）政權的人，就是「選民」；共同組裝起物體的東西，就是「成分」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with constituent.

example: The senator received thousands of letters from angry constituents opposing the new tax bill.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 constituent 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: voter is related, but constituent has its own usage pattern and context.
elector may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with constituent.

usage_note: constituent is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To compel or force someone toward a particular course of action; to severely restrict the scope, activity, or freedom of someone or something.
definition_zh: 限制；約束；強迫、迫使

mnemonic.story_en: Fewer funds will CONSTRAIN our budget, drawing it tight (STRINGERE) and completely (COM) stopping our growth.
mnemonic.story_zh: 完全（COM）用繩子拉緊勒死（STRINGERE），使對方毫無活動空間，這就是「限制、約束」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = completely; connect this root idea with constrain.

example: The lack of external funding will severely constrain the research team's ability to conduct long-term field trials.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 constrain 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: restrict is related, but constrain has its own usage pattern and context.
limit may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with constrain.

usage_note: constrain is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To look thoughtfully for a long time at something; to think profoundly or deeply about a potential future action.
definition_zh: 沉思；冥想；深思熟慮；盤算

mnemonic.story_en: Monks sit quietly to CONTEMPLATE life, transforming their minds into a peaceful TEMPLUM (temple/shrine).
mnemonic.story_zh: 字源與神殿（TEMPLUM）有關。想像古人在安靜的神殿中「完全（COM）」沉浸下來，對著上天「深思熟慮、冥想」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = completely; connect this root idea with contemplate.

example: The CEO decided to take a week off to contemplate the long-term future and restructuring of the company.

roots.meaning: shrine, space marked out for observation

example_zh: 這個例句展示 contemplate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: ponder is related, but contemplate has its own usage pattern and context.
meditate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with contemplate.

usage_note: contemplate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To deny the truth of a statement by asserting the opposite; to be in conflict or inconsistent with something else.
definition_zh: 反駁；與...矛盾；抵觸

mnemonic.story_en: It is rude to CONTRADICT your boss by DICING (speaking) directly CONTRA (against) his ideas in public.
mnemonic.story_zh: 對著（CONTRA）別人說（DICERE）相反的話，就是「反駁」；兩件事唱反調，就是「相矛盾」。
mnemonic.root_memory: CONTRA- = against, opposite; connect this root idea with contradict.

example: The new forensic evidence directly contradicts the suspect's original alibi statement.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 contradict 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: deny is related, but contradict has its own usage pattern and context.
oppose may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with contradict.

usage_note: contradict is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To come together or assemble for a formal meeting, activity, or official purpose; to cause to assemble.
definition_zh: 召集；召開（會議）；聚集

mnemonic.story_en: The prime minister will CONVENE parliament, asking all leaders to VENIRE (come) together (COM).
mnemonic.story_zh: 叫大家一起（COM）過來（VENIRE），通常用於官方場合「召開」會議或「召集」人員。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM- = together; connect this root idea with convene.

example: The United Nations Security Council will convene tomorrow morning to discuss the escalating crisis.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 convene 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: assemble is related, but convene has its own usage pattern and context.
summon may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with convene.

usage_note: convene is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Believing that people are motivated purely by self-interest; distrustful of human sincerity or integrity.
definition_zh: 憤世嫉俗的；犬儒主義的；懷疑人性本善的

mnemonic.story_en: A CYNICAL person has a bitter view of society, barking like a wild dog (KUON) at what they see as fake kindness.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自古希臘「犬儒學派」。他們認為世人皆虛偽自私，看穿一切般地對世俗抱持「憤世嫉俗、冷嘲熱熱」的態度。
mnemonic.root_memory: KUON = dog; connect this root idea with cynical.

example: Many young citizens have become cynical about politicians' empty promises during election campaigns.

roots.meaning_zh: 狗（源自希臘犬儒學派，嘲弄世俗）

example_zh: 這個例句展示 cynical 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: skeptical is related, but cynical has its own usage pattern and context.
distrustful may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with cynical.

usage_note: cynical is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Openly resisting or refusing to obey an authority, law, or rule; challenging a force deemed impossible to overcome.
definition_zh: 公然反抗；蔑視；挑釁（現在分詞形式）

mnemonic.story_en: By DEFYING the tyrant, the rebels were breaking (DIS) their FIDUS (faith/oath) to the corrupt crown.
mnemonic.story_zh: 解開或取消（DIS）過去對統治者的效忠與信任（FIDUS），站出來「公然反抗、蔑視」其權威。
mnemonic.root_memory: DIS- = undoing, away; connect this root idea with defying.

example: Defying the strict curfew, hundreds of protestors gathered in the central square at midnight.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 defying 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: resisting is related, but defying has its own usage pattern and context.
challenging may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with defying.

usage_note: defying is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To deny a person or place the possession or use of something, especially an essential need or right.
definition_zh: 剝奪；使喪失

mnemonic.story_en: To DEPRIVE a prisoner of sleep means to completely (DE) separate (PRIVARE) them from their normal rest.
mnemonic.story_zh: 徹底（DE）將某人和他應得的權利或物品分開、孤立（PRIVARE），這就是「剝奪」。
mnemonic.root_memory: DE- = completely, thoroughly; connect this root idea with deprive.

example: The continuous loud noise from the street below began to deprive the residents of sleep.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 deprive 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: strip is related, but deprive has its own usage pattern and context.
rob may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with deprive.

usage_note: deprive is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Careful and circumspect in one's speech or actions, especially in order to avoid causing offense or to gain an advantage; unobtrusive.
definition_zh: 謹慎的；考慮周到的；不引人注目的

mnemonic.story_en: A DISCREET butler knows how to discern (DISCERNERE) secrets and keep them quiet, never gossiping.
mnemonic.story_zh: 具備辨別（DISCERNERE）事理的能力，在外表現得「行事謹慎、不張揚」，絕不給人添麻煩。
mnemonic.root_memory: DISCERNERE = to separate, distinguish; connect this root idea with discreet.

example: The diplomat made a discreet inquiry about the political prisoner's health without alerting the press.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 discreet 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: cautious is related, but discreet has its own usage pattern and context.
circumspect may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with discreet.

usage_note: discreet is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To pull or twist out of shape; to give a misleading or false account or impression of a fact or reality.
definition_zh: 扭曲（形狀）；歪曲（事實、真相）

mnemonic.story_en: The corrupt media tried to DISTORT the truth by completely twisting (TORQ) the facts of the interview.
mnemonic.story_zh: 徹底（DIS）將事實像毛巾一樣扭轉（TORQ），使其偏離本來的面貌，即為「歪曲、扭曲」。
mnemonic.root_memory: DIS- = completely, thoroughly; connect this root idea with distort.

example: The legal defense argued that the prosecutor tried to distort the truth by presenting text messages out of context.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 distort 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: misrepresent is related, but distort has its own usage pattern and context.
falsify may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with distort.

usage_note: distort is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The state of being diverse; a range of different things; the practice of including people from a range of different social backgrounds.
definition_zh: 多樣性；多元化；差異性

mnemonic.story_en: To build cultural DIVERSITY, we must look at people who have turned (VERS) in completely different (DI) directions.
mnemonic.story_zh: 往不同的方向（DI）轉身（VERS），不拘泥於單一方向，展現出「多樣性、多元化」。
mnemonic.root_memory: DIS- = aside, apart; connect this root idea with diversity.

example: The university prides itself on the cultural diversity of its student body, with individuals from over 80 nations.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 diversity 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: variety is related, but diversity has its own usage pattern and context.
multiplicity may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with diversity.

usage_note: diversity is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To give official permission or legal power for someone to do something.
definition_zh: 授權；批准；准許

mnemonic.root_memory: AUCTOR = authority; authorize means giving someone authority to act.
mnemonic.story_en: The director AUTHORIZED the purchase after confirming that the budget allowed it.
mnemonic.story_zh: 主管確認預算允許後，「授權（AUTHORIZE）」這筆採購。

example: Only the project manager can authorize payments above the approved limit.
example_zh: 只有專案經理能核准超過已批准上限的付款。

near_synonyms.difference: allow is general; authorize implies official permission or authority.
approve means accept as satisfactory; authorize gives permission to proceed.

usage_note: authorize is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: The interest, support, or representation of another person or group, especially in the phrase on behalf of.
definition_zh: 代表；為了…的利益

mnemonic.root_memory: BEHALF suggests standing by someone’s side to represent them.
mnemonic.story_en: The lawyer spoke ON BEHALF of families who could not attend the hearing.
mnemonic.story_zh: 律師代表無法出席聽證會的家庭發言。

example: I am writing on behalf of the committee to thank you for your contribution.
example_zh: 我代表委員會寫信感謝你的貢獻。

near_synonyms.difference: instead of means replacing someone; on behalf of means representing their interests.
for is broad; on behalf of is more formal and representative.

usage_note: behalf is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: Involving two sides, parties, or countries; affecting both sides of a body or relationship.
definition_zh: 雙邊的；雙側的

mnemonic.root_memory: BI = two and LATERAL = side; bilateral involves two sides.
mnemonic.story_en: The two governments signed a BILATERAL trade agreement after months of talks.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩國政府經過數月談判後簽署「雙邊（BILATERAL）」貿易協定。

example: The treaty created a bilateral framework for sharing security information.
example_zh: 該條約建立了共享安全資訊的雙邊架構。

near_synonyms.difference: multilateral involves several parties; bilateral involves exactly two.
mutual stresses reciprocity; bilateral stresses two parties or sides.

usage_note: bilateral is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: The ability, power, or capacity to do something, especially at an organizational, technical, or personal level.
definition_zh: 能力；性能；可完成某事的條件

mnemonic.root_memory: CAP = take or hold; capability is what someone can handle or do.
mnemonic.story_en: The new software expanded the team’s CAPABILITY to analyze large datasets.
mnemonic.story_zh: 新軟體擴大了團隊分析大型資料集的「能力（CAPABILITY）」。

example: The country is investing in cyber capabilities to protect critical infrastructure.
example_zh: 該國正投資網路能力以保護關鍵基礎設施。

near_synonyms.difference: capacity often stresses maximum amount; capability stresses ability to perform.
skill is learned personal ability; capability can belong to people, systems, or institutions.

usage_note: capability is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: To arrange people, things, or information into groups according to shared features or official categories.
definition_zh: 分類；歸類；列為機密

mnemonic.root_memory: CLASS + FAC = make into a class; classify means putting things into categories.
mnemonic.story_en: Researchers CLASSIFIED the responses by age, income, and education level.
mnemonic.story_zh: 研究人員依年齡、收入和教育程度將回覆「分類（CLASSIFY）」。

example: The documents were classified as confidential for national security reasons.
example_zh: 這些文件因國家安全理由被列為機密。

near_synonyms.difference: label means attach a name; classify means place within a system of categories.
rank orders by level; classify groups by shared features.

usage_note: classify is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: To happen at the same time or to match closely in position, opinion, or result.
definition_zh: 同時發生；一致；相符

mnemonic.root_memory: CO + INCIDE = fall together; events that coincide happen at the same time.
mnemonic.story_en: The conference COINCIDED with a major election, so attendance was lower than expected.
mnemonic.story_zh: 會議與重大選舉「同時發生（COINCIDE）」，因此出席人數低於預期。

example: Her conclusions coincide with the findings of several earlier studies.
example_zh: 她的結論與幾項早期研究結果相符。

near_synonyms.difference: overlap means share part of a range; coincide means match or occur together.
agree often refers to people or opinions; coincide can refer to events, data, or positions.

usage_note: coincide is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: Consisting of many connected parts and therefore difficult to understand, analyze, or solve.
definition_zh: 複雜的；錯綜的；複合的

mnemonic.root_memory: COM + PLECT = woven together; complex things have many parts woven together.
mnemonic.story_en: The policy problem was COMPLEX because it involved law, economics, and public trust.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這項政策問題很「複雜（COMPLEX）」，因為牽涉法律、經濟與公共信任。

example: The team developed a model to explain complex interactions among climate variables.
example_zh: 團隊建立模型來解釋氣候變項之間的複雜互動。

near_synonyms.difference: complicated stresses difficulty; complex stresses many interrelated parts.
difficult is broad; complex specifically involves multiple connected elements.

usage_note: complex is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: To act according to a rule, request, law, or standard.
definition_zh: 遵守；服從；依從

mnemonic.root_memory: COMPLY originally links to completing what is required; to comply is to meet a rule.
mnemonic.story_en: The company had to COMPLY with safety regulations before reopening the factory.
mnemonic.story_zh: 公司必須「遵守（COMPLY）」安全規定後才能重新開放工廠。

example: All applicants must comply with the documentation requirements listed online.
example_zh: 所有申請者都必須遵守網路上列出的文件要求。

near_synonyms.difference: conform means fit a standard or expectation; comply means obey a specific rule or request.
submit can mean yield; comply stresses acting according to requirements.

usage_note: comply is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: A state in which opposing forces or influences are perfectly balanced; a calm state of mind.
definition_zh: 平衡；均衡；（心情的）平靜

mnemonic.story_en: To maintain EQUILIBRIUM, the scientist ensured both sides of the scale were AEQUUS (equal) on the LIBRA (balance).
mnemonic.story_zh: 天平（LIBRA，也是天秤座的由來）兩邊達到了等同（AEQUUS）的分量，呈現完美的「平衡、狀態穩定」。
mnemonic.root_memory: AEQUUS = equal; connect this root idea with equilibrium.

example: Yoga helps practitioners restore their internal equilibrium and release accumulated stress.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 equilibrium 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: balance is related, but equilibrium has its own usage pattern and context.
stability may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with equilibrium.

usage_note: equilibrium is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: One part of a larger system, machine, argument, or process.
definition_zh: 組成部分；零件；要素

mnemonic.root_memory: COMPONENTS are pieces placed together to form a system.
mnemonic.story_en: The engine failed because one small COMPONENT had been installed incorrectly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 引擎故障是因為一個小「零件（COMPONENT）」安裝錯誤。

example: Trust is a key component of successful long-term cooperation.
example_zh: 信任是長期合作成功的關鍵要素。

near_synonyms.difference: element is a basic part; component often belongs to a larger working system.
ingredient is used for mixtures or food; component is broader and technical.

usage_note: component is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: A substance, word, or structure formed by combining two or more elements; as a verb, to make something more intense or complicated.
definition_zh: 化合物；複合詞；複合體；加劇

mnemonic.root_memory: COM + POUND means placed together; a compound is formed from joined parts.
mnemonic.story_en: Water is a chemical COMPOUND made of hydrogen and oxygen.
mnemonic.story_zh: 水是由氫和氧組成的化學「化合物（COMPOUND）」。

example: The error was compounded by poor communication between departments.
example_zh: 部門間溝通不良使這個錯誤更加嚴重。

near_synonyms.difference: mixture may be physically blended; compound often implies a more defined combination.
complex describes difficulty; compound names something formed from parts.

usage_note: compound is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge concerned with these; avoiding injury to others or environment.
definition_zh: 倫理的；道德的；合乎道德的

mnemonic.story_en: An ETHICAL doctor must always follow the high ETHOS (moral values) established by the medical community.
mnemonic.story_zh: 源自希臘文的 ETHOS（精神特質、道德）。指行為必須符合社會的「道德與倫理規範」。
mnemonic.root_memory: ETHOS = custom, moral character; connect this root idea with ethical.

example: The committee is reviewing whether the medical experiment was ethical and protected patient safety.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 ethical 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: moral is related, but ethical has its own usage pattern and context.
principled may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with ethical.

usage_note: ethical is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To escape or avoid something, especially by cleverness or trickery; to elude a moral or legal duty.
definition_zh: 逃避；規避（法律、責任、稅收）

mnemonic.story_en: To EVADE taxes, the criminal tried to walk away (VADERE) from his legal duty and out (EX) of the system.
mnemonic.story_zh: 看到危險或責任，趕快往外（EX）跨步走開（VADERE）以免被抓到，引申為「逃避、規避」。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX- = out, away; connect this root idea with evade.

example: The billionaire was arrested after a hidden bank account revealed he tried to evade taxes for a decade.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 evade 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: avoid is related, but evade has its own usage pattern and context.
elude may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with evade.

usage_note: evade is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To bring or recall a feeling, memory, or image to the conscious mind; to elicit a response.
definition_zh: 喚起（記憶、情感）；引起（共鳴、強烈反應）

mnemonic.story_en: Old black-and-white photos often EVOKE strong nostalgia, calling (VOCARE) out (EX) long-lost childhood memories.
mnemonic.story_zh: 把深藏在潛意識底下的眼淚或記憶，大聲地召喚（VOCARE）出來（EX），使人「喚起、引起」某種情緒。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX- = out, forth; connect this root idea with evoke.

example: The smell of fresh pine leaves never failed to evoke childhood memories of camping trips in her mind.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 evoke 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: elicit is related, but evoke has its own usage pattern and context.
provoke may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with evoke.

usage_note: evoke is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The process or state of excluding or being excluded from a place, group, privilege, or consideration.
definition_zh: 排除；排斥；除外

mnemonic.story_en: The club's EXCLUSION of non-members meant they would shut (CLAUDERE) the door on them and keep them out (EX).
mnemonic.story_zh: 把不符合資格的人推到門外（EX），然後狠狠把大門關上（CLAUDERE）不准他們進來，就是「排斥、排除」。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX- = out; connect this root idea with exclusion.

example: The systematic exclusion of women from high-level corporate boards led to a massive civil lawsuit.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 exclusion 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: omission is related, but exclusion has its own usage pattern and context.
rejection may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with exclusion.

usage_note: exclusion is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To calculate a number, result, or value using mathematics or a computer.
definition_zh: 計算；運算

mnemonic.root_memory: PUTARE = calculate; compute means calculating carefully, often by machine.
mnemonic.story_en: The program COMPUTES the average score automatically after all results are entered.
mnemonic.story_zh: 所有結果輸入後，程式會自動「計算（COMPUTE）」平均分數。

example: The system can compute risk scores in real time from transaction data.
example_zh: 該系統能根據交易資料即時計算風險分數。

near_synonyms.difference: estimate gives an approximate value; compute suggests calculation.
measure obtains data; compute processes data mathematically.

usage_note: compute is common in formal or academic English; use the collocations to choose the right context.

definition: Free from an obligation, duty, or liability imposed on others by law or authority.
definition_zh: 免除的；豁免的

mnemonic.story_en: Since she has a health condition, she is EXEMPT from military service, taken out (EX) of the draft list (EMERE).
mnemonic.story_zh: 被從義務清單中挑選出來（EMERE）並移到外頭（EX），使其享有「免除、豁免」的特權。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX- = out; connect this root idea with exempt.

example: Charitable organizations are typically exempt from paying federal income taxes.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 exempt 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: excused is related, but exempt has its own usage pattern and context.
immune may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with exempt.

usage_note: exempt is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Originating in or characteristic of a distant foreign country, especially when excitingly strange or unusual.
definition_zh: 異國風情的；外來的；奇特的

mnemonic.story_en: The zoo bought several EXOTIC birds that came from a tropical jungle way outside (EXO) our country.
mnemonic.story_zh: 字根 EXO 代表外面（如外骨骼 exoskeleton）。來自遙遠國界「外面（EXO）」的動植物或文化，給人一種「異國風情、奇特」的感覺。
mnemonic.root_memory: EXO = outside; connect this root idea with exotic.

example: The restaurant specializes in exotic spices imported directly from remote islands in Indonesia.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 exotic 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: foreign is related, but exotic has its own usage pattern and context.
alien may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with exotic.

usage_note: exotic is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.
